items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of methane with chlorine in bright sunlight and name the type of reaction.

rubric.why: The equation identifies the reactants and the substitution products.
rubric.description: Writes the correct reaction equation or identifies its reactants and products.
rubric.how: Award for the balanced equation or for correctly naming all reactants and products.

items.followUp: Write three differences between Rutherford's and Bohr's atomic models.

rubric.why: This compares the electron paths proposed in the two models.
rubric.description: Contrasts Rutherford's lack of fixed orbits with Bohr's fixed orbits.
rubric.how: Award for stating both sides of this contrast.

rubric.why: This compares the electron energies allowed in the two models.
rubric.description: Contrasts Rutherford's non-quantized electron energies with Bohr's quantized energy levels.
rubric.how: Award for stating both sides of this contrast.

rubric.why: This compares whether orbiting electrons lose energy in each model.
rubric.description: Contrasts radiation by orbiting electrons in Rutherford's model with no radiation in Bohr's stationary orbits.
rubric.how: Award for stating both sides of this contrast.

rubric.why: This compares the models' explanations of atomic stability.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford's model could not explain atomic stability, whereas Bohr's model explained it.

accept: could not explain the line spectrum
rubric.why: This compares the models' ability to explain atomic spectra.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford's model could not explain line spectra, whereas Bohr's model explained the hydrogen spectrum.

modelAnswer: Rutherford proposed no fixed orbits for electrons, whereas Bohr proposed fixed orbits.
Rutherford's model did not have quantized electron energies, whereas Bohr's model has quantized energy levels.
In Rutherford's model, an orbiting electron radiates energy; in Bohr's model, an electron does not radiate energy in a stationary orbit.
Rutherford's model could not explain atomic stability, whereas Bohr's model explained atomic stability.
Rutherford's model could not explain the line spectrum of hydrogen, whereas Bohr's model explained the hydrogen spectrum.
